# Johor Darul Ta'zim FC (JDT) — full brief

Johor Darul Ta'zim FC (JDT), the Southern Tigers, is Johor's professional football club, playing at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Iskandar Puteri, Malaysia.

## Facts with sources
- 12 consecutive Malaysia Super League titles (https://www.nst.com.my/amp/sports/football/2026/08/1513860/jdt-drawn-alongside-asean-rivals-and-k-league-opposition-acle)
- First Malaysian club to win a continental title (AFC Cup 2015) (https://johorsoutherntigers.my/)
- First Malaysian club to reach the AFC Champions League Elite quarter-finals (2025/26) (https://theiskandarian.com/johor-darul-tazim-made-it-to-afc-champions-league-elites-quarter-finals/)
- Only Malaysian club academy with AFC Two-Star Academy Accreditation, with teams from Under-12 to Under-23 (https://www.nst.com.my/amp/sports/football/2026/08/1520540/jdts-youth-pipeline-keeps-producing-champions)
- 15 of the 23 players in Malaysia's 2026 ASEAN U-19 squad came from JDT III and JDT IV (https://www.bernama.com/en/news.php?id=2563079)
- Sultan Ibrahim Stadium opened in 2020 and holds 40,000 fans (https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/malaysia-match-added-to-blues-pre-season-2026)

## Next-gen Tigers: the JDT academy pathway
The JDT academy is the club's youth system, with teams from Under-12 to Under-23 and senior reserve sides JDT II to JDT V. It is the only Malaysian club academy with AFC Two-Star Academy Accreditation, and it supplies players to Malaysia's age-group national teams.
- Age-group teams from Under-12 to Under-23
- Reserve and development sides JDT II, JDT III, JDT IV and JDT V
- AFC Two-Star Academy Accreditation, the only one held by a Malaysian club academy
- A track record of supplying national age-group squads: 15 of 23 players in Malaysia's 2026 ASEAN U-19 squad

Q: How many age groups does the JDT academy have?
A: According to the club's academy leadership, JDT runs the only fully professional Malaysian club academy, with teams from Under-12 up to Under-23. Above the academy sit the senior development sides JDT II, JDT III, JDT IV and JDT V, each with its own roster on the club website.

Q: Is the JDT academy accredited?
A: Yes. JDT is the only Malaysian club academy that holds AFC Two-Star Academy Accreditation from the Asian Football Confederation, which recognises a structured and continuous approach to player development across age groups.

Q: Do JDT academy players play for Malaysia?
A: Yes. When Malaysia named its 23-player squad for the 2026 ASEAN Under-19 Championship, 15 players came from JDT: eight from JDT III and seven from JDT IV, according to the Football Association of Malaysia's announcement reported by Bernama.

Q: How can my child get a trial at JDT?
A: Trial dates and requirements are announced by the club. Follow the official JDT website news section and the club's social channels for academy announcements, and contact the club through its official contact page for current trial information.

## Johor pride: a family matchday tradition
A JDT home match is a Johor family occasion: Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Iskandar Puteri seats 40,000, has prayer rooms, and has served local favourites such as bubur lambuk and mee kawah to fans on big European and Asian nights.
- A 40,000-capacity stadium opened in 2020
- Prayer rooms and modern amenities, as noted at the 2025 ACL Elite match
- Local food on matchday, such as bubur lambuk and mee kawah served at the JDT vs Buriram match
- Premium options: 12 corporate boxes and two premium lounges added for the 2025-26 season

Q: Is Sultan Ibrahim Stadium suitable for families?
A: Sultan Ibrahim Stadium opened in 2020 with modern facilities, including prayer rooms, according to a Bernama report. With 40,000 seats it is a large venue, so families should arrive early, check the club's ground regulations before travelling and agree a meeting point with children.

Q: What food is available at a JDT match?
A: Food varies by match. For the 2025 AFC Champions League Elite match against Buriram United, Bernama reported that local dishes such as bubur lambuk and mee kawah were prepared for fans at the stadium. Check club announcements before each match for current food options.

Q: Where is the JDT stadium?
A: JDT play at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Iskandar Puteri (Gelang Patah, 81120), Johor, Malaysia. The stadium opened in 2020 and is the home ground of the Southern Tigers.

Q: Are there premium seats for families or groups?
A: Yes. Before the 2025-26 season the club completed upgrades that added 12 corporate boxes and two premium lounges at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, as reported by Malay Mail. Contact the club for availability and pricing.

## Matchday made easy: tickets, gates and kick-off
Buy JDT tickets through the club's official ticketing partner Tickethotline, check fixtures and kick-off times on the official JDT schedule page, and read the ground regulations before travelling to Sultan Ibrahim Stadium. Big matches can sell out online.
- Official tickets through Tickethotline
- Fixtures, results and standings on the official JDT website
- Ground regulations published by the club
- Sold-out notices for high-demand matches, such as the 2026 Charity Shield

Q: Where can I buy official JDT tickets?
A: JDT match tickets are sold through Tickethotline (tickethotline.com.my), the ticketing platform the club uses for home fixtures and special matches such as the 2026 friendly against Chelsea. Buying from the official channel avoids counterfeit or resale risk.

Q: Where do I check JDT fixtures and kick-off times?
A: The official JDT website lists the Southern Tigers' schedule, results and league standings. Kick-off times can change for broadcast or continental fixtures, so check the schedule page and the club's social channels again on the day of the match.

Q: Do JDT matches sell out?
A: Yes, high-demand matches do. The 2026 Charity Shield against Selangor FC sold out online, according to The Iskandarian, and continental nights draw some of the biggest crowds of the season. Buy early for big fixtures.

Q: What are the stadium rules?
A: The club publishes ground regulations for Sultan Ibrahim Stadium on its official website. Read them before travelling, as they cover what supporters may bring into the stadium and expected conduct on matchday.

## FAQ

Q: What is Johor Darul Ta'zim FC?
A: Johor Darul Ta'zim FC (JDT), the Southern Tigers, is Johor's professional football club. It plays at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Iskandar Puteri and has won 12 consecutive Malaysia Super League titles, according to the New Straits Times.

Q: Where does JDT play home matches?
A: JDT play at Sultan Ibrahim Stadium in Iskandar Puteri (Gelang Patah), Johor. The stadium opened in 2020 and holds 40,000 fans, making it one of the largest football venues in Malaysia.

Q: How do I buy JDT tickets?
A: Official JDT tickets are sold through Tickethotline (tickethotline.com.my). Check the official JDT fixtures page for upcoming matches and buy early for high-demand fixtures, which can sell out online.

Q: Does JDT have a youth academy?
A: Yes. JDT runs a fully professional academy with teams from Under-12 to Under-23, plus development sides JDT II to JDT V. It is the only Malaysian club academy with AFC Two-Star Academy Accreditation.

Q: What has JDT won?
A: JDT have won 12 straight Malaysia Super League titles and multiple Malaysia Cup and FA Cup trophies. In 2015 they became the first Malaysian club to win a continental title, the AFC Cup, as stated on the club website.

Q: How far has JDT gone in Asia?
A: In the 2025/26 AFC Champions League Elite, JDT became the first Malaysian club to reach the quarter-finals, after beating Sanfrecce Hiroshima in the round of 16, as reported by The Iskandarian.

Q: Where can I buy official JDT merchandise?
A: Official merchandise is sold through the JDT online store at store.johorsoutherntigers.com.my and at JDT Direct, the club's official merchandise outlet listed on the official website.

Q: Is a JDT match suitable for families?
A: Yes. Sultan Ibrahim Stadium has modern facilities including prayer rooms, and big matches have featured local food such as bubur lambuk and mee kawah. Families should arrive early and read the club's ground regulations.
